note: MOV-013: #[spec_only]/#[ext(spec_only)] on a public/public(package)/public(friend)/entry function ships in production bytecode -- the Move compiler does not strip it, unlike #[test_only]. Regression fixture is the advisory draft's own probe::vault module verbatim: leak_secret and set_owner both fire HIGH (they read/write a struct field), test_only_helper does not fire at all. Pins the negatives (a private #[spec_only] fun, #[ext(spec_only)] form), the MEDIUM severity band (no field touch, and a Move-2024 dot-CALL correctly not mistaken for a field touch), the attribute-attach discipline (no distance-window leak onto an unrelated item), and a 40,000-char identifier completing well inside a generous timing ceiling. Deliberately an independent scanner rather than a move-parser.mjs/parseModule() consumer: parseModule() measured 5583ms on this fork's unpatched move-parser.mjs at 40,000 characters (the quadratic fix landed on a separate branch in the sibling room, not this fork, and this unit's rails do not authorize touching move-parser.mjs) -- consuming it would have made this new rule inherit a live O(n^2) DoS on commit. INSPECT bounce, fixed: F1/HIGH -- spec_only as a comma-list member or a stacked second #[...] group on one line bypassed detection entirely (a one-token bypass of a HIGH-advisory rule); fixed by scanning every #[...] group on the line and treating spec_only as a member, not only the group's whole content -- all three bypass shapes plus the twelve surviving control shapes are pinned. F2/MEDIUM -- an unterminated function body scanned to EOF and was re-walked a second time for its field-touch check, so N unterminated bodies cost O(N x lines) (measured 50/166/669/2576ms at N=500/1000/2000/4000); folded into one bounded pass (MAX_BODY_SCAN_LINES=200, re-measured after a first, too-generous 5000-line attempt was found still quadratic at this N) -- re-measured 51/90/197/385ms, linear, pinned at N=4000 under a loose ceiling.
